title: Collecting {{term:data}}, tallies and pictograms
summary: Ask the class, count with tally marks and draw a pictogram.
guide: This studio follows Year 2 statistics: tally charts, simple tables and pictograms. Read the sentences aloud if your child is still learning to read.
{{term:tally}} marks: one line for each answer. The fifth line goes across the other four, so the marks come in groups of five. Groups of five are quicker to count: 5, 10, then the rest.
In a {{term:pictogram}} one picture can stand for more than one thing. The key under the chart says how many. If one picture stands for 2, half a picture stands for 1.
Charts always run from left to right.

engine.label-remove: Rub out a tally mark for {c}
engine.instruction-sort: Tap a card, then its row.

tally-survey.title: Make a tally
tally-survey.prompt: We asked 15 children: "Which fruit do you like best?" Guess which fruit will win. Now tap each card, then tap the row for that fruit to add a tally mark.
tally-survey.hint: Go through the cards in order. One card, one tally mark. Counted cards are crossed out.
tally-survey.success: Well done! Apple 6, banana 3, orange 4 and grapes 2. Apple wins.
tally-survey.why: Why does the fifth tally mark go across the other four?
tally-survey.model: So the marks come in groups of five. Then I don't have to count them one by one: one group is 5, and 5 and 1 more is 6.

feedback.empty: Tap a card, then the row for that fruit.
feedback.cards-left: Some cards are not counted yet. Count every card that is not crossed out.
feedback.tally-few: You missed a card. Look again.
feedback.tally-many: You counted a card twice. Use the − button to rub out a mark.
feedback.tally-wrong: A card is in the wrong row. Rub it out with − and put it in the right row.

count-tallies.title: Count the tallies
count-tallies.prompt: We asked a class which season they were born in. Count the tally marks and write the total for each row.
count-tallies.hint: Each crossed group is 5. Count the groups first: 5, 10, … then add the single marks.
count-tallies.success: That's right! Spring 7, summer 5, autumn 9 and winter 4.
count-tallies.why: In which season were most children born? How do you know?
count-tallies.model: Autumn, with 9 children. 9 is more than 7, 5 and 4. The autumn tally is also the longest.

feedback.empty: Write the total for each row.
feedback.count-empty: One row has no total yet.
feedback.gate-as-four: Count the line across too. Each group has 4 lines standing up and 1 across: that's 5.
feedback.count-wrong: One total is not right. Count the groups in fives, then the single marks.

build-pictogram.title: Build a pictogram
build-pictogram.prompt: Draw a pictogram of the fruit survey. Each ☺ stands for 2 children. Use the + and − buttons; each tap adds or takes away half a picture.
build-pictogram.hint: Apple is 6: 2 and 2 and 2, so 3 pictures. Banana is 3: one whole picture (2) and half a picture (1).
build-pictogram.success: Well done! With the key "one picture = 2 children" the pictogram is shorter and still right.
build-pictogram.why: Why did you draw half a picture for banana?
build-pictogram.model: Each picture stands for 2 children and 3 children like banana. 2 children make one whole picture and 1 is left over; 1 is half of 2, so it is half a picture.

feedback.key-ignored: You drew one picture for each child. But each picture stands for 2 children! So you need half as many pictures.
feedback.half-needed: That number is odd. One child is half a picture. Don't forget the half picture.
feedback.too-high: One row has too many pictures. Each picture is 2 children: count in twos.
feedback.too-low: One row has too few pictures. Each picture is 2 children: count in twos.

read-pictogram.title: Read a pictogram
read-pictogram.prompt: Ali, Sara, Maryam and Reza picked apples. Each picture stands for 2 apples. How many more apples did Maryam pick than Sara?
read-pictogram.hint: First count each child's apples: each picture is 2 and half a picture is 1. Then take the smaller number from the bigger one.
read-pictogram.success: That's right! Maryam picked 10 apples and Sara picked 5. 10 − 5 = 5
read-pictogram.why: Why is the answer 5 and not the number of extra pictures?
read-pictogram.model: Maryam has 5 pictures and Sara has 2 and a half. The difference is 2 and a half pictures. Each picture is 2 apples, so 2 pictures are 4 apples and half a picture is 1 apple: 5 apples altogether.

feedback.counted-pictures: You counted the pictures. But each picture stands for 2 apples! Count the apples first.
feedback.not-difference: That is all of Maryam's apples. We want to know how many more she picked than Sara.
feedback.added: You added the apples together. "How many more" means take away: Maryam's apples minus Sara's apples.
feedback.too-big: Too many. Count each child's apples again: each picture is 2, half a picture is 1.
feedback.too-small: Too few. Count each child's apples again: each picture is 2, half a picture is 1.
